clue.text: Certainly not an original idea

parts.note: an idea that comes later rather than first is, in one sense, not original: it is a later addition to the plan

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on somebody's derivative suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion that occurs to someone only later, as an addition, is by its timing not the first idea.

clue.text: Unyielding Scottish architect and soldier, perhaps

parts.note: Robert Adam was the celebrated eighteenth-century Scottish architect
a soldier is one kind of ant, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A stubborn Scottish designer is paired with a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like an army man, but soldier ants are a caste of ant, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone refusing to give way is firmly insistent, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Clan emblem many carry aloft

indicators.note: in this down clue the carrying word sits up above the 'many' letter, held aloft by it

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a crossword 'many'

explanation.surface: A tribal symbol is borne high by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'aloft' puts TOTE above M, as if M were holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a sacred object or image adopted as the symbol of a tribe or kin group.

clue.text: Disturbed near court, his relations may be 26

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unsettled near a law court whose accounts may be of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' means things related, i.e. tales told; 26 across is ANECDOTAL, so this teller's stories are anecdotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled storyteller recounts anecdotes, so his tellings are naturally of that kind.

clue.text: Back-slapping male with cultural pretensions

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
arty describes someone affecting an interest in the arts

explanation.surface: A jovial man who fancies himself a connoisseur.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudly cheerful, back-slapping manner is described as bluff and jolly.

clue.text: Make rare opening in Government for weaker party

parts.note: to underdo meat is to cook it too little, making it rare

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from the word Government

explanation.surface: Instructions to steer a government's beginnings in favour of the less powerful side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' looks like 'uncommon', but it is the cooking sense: underdone.
explanation.definitionFit: In any contest the side expected to lose is the one at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Mediocre press cuttings?

definitions.meaning: second-rate journalists are dismissively called the hired writers of Fleet Street
cuts or gashes, and press cuttings suggest newspapers too

explanation.surface: A sneer at second-rate newspaper clippings.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists of little talent are disparagingly named after hired drudges, and rough chops or cuts share the same word.

clue.text: Not all are established, say, as county

parts.note: some means a part, not the whole

indicators.note: say signals that the preceding word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: the word are spoken sounds like the letter R
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: A remark that only some things are settled in a particular county.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England, so the answer is an example of one.

clue.text: Some host endeavours to provide port

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A host does his best to serve a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'to provide port' was trimmed: 'to provide' is a link, and only 'port' can stand in for the answer. 'port' looks like the wine but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian harbour town on the North Sea coast, an example of a seaport.

clue.text: Bizarre action in opposition to opening of cinema

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here from the word cinema

explanation.surface: A strange stunt staged in protest at a new picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a grotesque or absurd piece of behaviour, a caper.

clue.text: Impudent bounder, returning with gold, promises to pay

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: returning means the word for bounder is read backwards

parts.note: a cad and a bounder are both old words for a dishonourable man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A cheeky rogue comes back with gold and a fistful of IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and disrespectful behaviour is called brazen or cheeky.

clue.text: Sound tool for cutting church carpet

indicators.note: Sound tells us the tool's name is heard rather than spelt, losing its silent final letter

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
a minster is a large or important church

explanation.surface: A reliable chopper for cutting a church's flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'reliable', describing the tool, but signals the homophone. Axminster is a Devon town famous for its carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven pile carpet named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Jumblies' unseaworthy craft is put about by first mate

indicators.note: a ship put about turns round, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Eve, in Genesis, was the first wife, the mate of Adam

explanation.surface: A leaky boat from a nonsense poem is turned round by its senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem The Jumblies, the Jumblies 'went to sea in a Sieve'. 'first mate' suggests a ship's officer but means Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's Jumblies sailed in a perforated kitchen utensil, which no boat-builder would call seaworthy.

clue.text: Sweet drink's cold — replaced by hot ultimately

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter gives way to another in the drink's name

parts.note: coffee is a drink; the 's is 'has', a link
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word hot

explanation.surface: A beverage that has gone cold is swapped for a hot one in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Regulator with knowing wife is contemptible person

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
a heel is a cad or contemptible person

explanation.surface: A man who controls things has a shrewd wife and is despised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' as an adjective, meaning shrewd or wide awake, is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A flywheel is a heavy wheel that smooths and regulates a machine's speed.

clue.text: Collected, like the works of Beethoven

definitions.meaning: collected in the sense of calm and self-possessed
Beethoven's works were written, i.e. set down in music by him

explanation.surface: A complete edition of Beethoven's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calm is self-possessed, and music that a composer wrote was created by him.

clue.text: Slug taken by blackbird in deep hollow

parts.note: to slug is to punch hard
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A garden pest is eaten by a blackbird in a deep valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden pest but is a blow; 'blackbird' must be split into black and bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbowl is a bowl-shaped depression in hills, like the Devil's Punch Bowl in Surrey.

clue.text: Deed central to upset of corporation dogsbody

indicators.note: central to puts the deed's word in the middle of the next piece
upset in a down clue turns the little word of upside down

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a deed
corporation is old jocular British slang for a large belly, as is tum

explanation.surface: An action at the heart of upending a company's lowly worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company, but is old British slang for a paunch, which makes the TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant who does every menial job is a factotum, a dogsbody.

clue.text: What occurs during siesta in castle in Spain?

definitions.meaning: an afternoon nap brings a dream in the daytime
a castle in Spain is an idiom for an unrealisable fantasy

explanation.surface: Wondering what happens during an afternoon nap in a Spanish fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in Spain is a wishful fancy, and a reverie dreamed in daylight fits a nap too.

clue.text: Daughter had up, having pinched rings and small trinket

indicators.note: having pinched means holding something stolen inside, so the rings go within
up in a down clue reads the word had from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped, so two rings give two Os

explanation.surface: A daughter was arrested for stealing rings and a little bauble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like arrested, but it means holding something inside, so the rings sit within the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is a casual word for any small gadget or thingummy whose name escapes one.

clue.text: Popular move, building arch

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a step is a move

explanation.surface: A well-received manoeuvre in constructing an archway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' suggests architecture, but it is the arch of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle part of the foot.

clue.text: Game in which score can just be beaten

definitions.text: Game in which score can just be beaten

parts.words: Game in which score can just be beaten
parts.note: a score is twenty, and in this card game the target is twenty-one, one more

explanation.surface: A contest where the points tally can narrowly be topped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' is twenty, not the points tally; in this card game, also called vingt-et-un or blackjack, the winning total is 21.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is the British card game, also known as twenty-one, aiming for a total of 21.

clue.text: Draw level and come to a stop, either way

definitions.meaning: to draw level with another car is to come alongside it
a driver halts by drawing in to the kerb

explanation.surface: A driver comes alongside and then halts, whichever direction he faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either way' adds that the letters read the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A car halting, or another closing the gap to come alongside, both use the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Additional trouble after head has left

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which here departs

parts.note: bother means trouble

explanation.surface: More difficulty arises once the boss has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or additional, as in 'one other thing'.

clue.text: Staff originally employed organising Wild West display

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: originally takes the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Employees first hired to stage a cowboy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of cowboy skills such as bronco riding, associated with the American West.

clue.text: Land in border county

parts.note: to touch is to border on
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Ground lying in a frontier county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's landing is called its touchdown.

clue.text: Group of players taking 31 days over movie

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, places the month above the film

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated Oct
E.T. is Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: A band takes a month off for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a musical ensemble of eight performers.

clue.text: Like some stories, can lead to novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, signalling a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A tin may give rise to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal accounts are short personal tales, so some stories are of this kind.

clue.text: Perform better than United in scoreless draw

indicators.note: in places the team inside the drawn score

parts.note: a scoreless draw is nil-nil, written as two zeros, here letter Os
Utd is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A football team beats expectations in a goalless game.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass or beat someone at something.

clue.text: International firm's complaint about government cut

parts.note: Co is a firm, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: about means going around the next piece

parts.note: a moan is a complaint

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a polity is a form of government

explanation.surface: A global company's grievance concerns government cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitan means belonging to all parts of the world, international.
